P1b.reply:
I recognise this as the eye-tracking data from the "Predicting Relevance Based on Eye Movements" challenge, the PASCAL / NIPS 2005 workshop "Inferring Relevance from Eye Movements" (Salojärvi et al., Helsinki University of Technology). Its features include lineNo, assgNo, prevFixDur, firstfixDur and so on. The data are also on OpenML as "eye_movements" (ID 1044), and the task is to classify each word as irrelevant, relevant or the correct answer.

calls.reply:
I'm working from memory of the data set's structure, not from the data, so these scores are rough guesses.

As I recall, the eye-movement data has 27 features in the original ordering: the first columns are numberOfPredictedRegressions, numberOfPredictedFixations, and so on, and the later columns are the ones that characterize fixations. OpenML 1044 appears to have 20 features after some were dropped. The names I remember are:

- Early columns: nrSacc, nrFix, meanFixDur, meanPupilDiam
- Others: regressions, firstPassFixDur, ... and so on.
- Later columns: the "feature" variables such as fixDur and the regression-related ones.

I can't map indices to names reliably. The class is relevance of the title: irrelevant, relevant, or correct answer. The features are all weak predictors, and accuracy is typically around 0.5–0.6. The ones that tend to matter are the regression-related and fixation-duration features, plus the pupil diameter features.

Since I can't tell which index is which, I'll spread the scores in a narrow band, giving slightly higher values to the middle and later features.
